itens.titulo: Q2 earnings recap: Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) tops processors and graphics chips stocks
itens.descricao: Q2 earnings recap: Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) tops processors and graphics chips stocks Yahoo Finance
trechos: Let's take a look at how processors and graphics chips stocks fared in Q2, starting with Intel (NASDAQ:INTC).

The biggest demand drivers for processors (CPUs) and graphics chips at the moment are secular trends related to 5G and Internet of Things, autonomous driving, and high performance computing in the data center space, specifically around AI and machine learning.
The 8 processors and graphics chips stocks we track reported a very strong Q2.
As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 5.2% while next quarter's revenue guidance was 6.8% above.
On average, they are down 10.5% since the latest earnings results.

Best Q2: Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) Inventor of the x86 processor that powered decades of technological innovation in PCs, data centers, and numerous other markets, Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) is a leading manufacturer of computer processors and graphics chips.
Intel reported revenues of $16.13 billion, up 25.4% year on year.
This print exceeded analysts' expectations by 11.7%.

itens.titulo: Will Alphabet Stock Surge After Oct. 28?
itens.descricao: Will Alphabet Stock Surge After Oct. 28? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) reports Q3 2026 earnings after the market closes on Oct.
Wall Street analysts have an average revenue estimate of $127.8 billion, which would be a 25% year-over-year increase, and earnings per share (EPS) of $3.
Last quarter, Alphabet easily surpassed revenue expectations -- and its share price still ended up falling 7% the next day.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
Its moves this year have been significant, closing up 10% after its April 29 report, and down 7.1% after its July 22 report.
Stretching it to the last 16 quarters, Alphabet has closed up seven times and closed down nine times.
The average move is 5.2% in either direction.

itens.titulo: UBS on Amazon: Street’s AWS margin estimates for 2027 are too low
itens.descricao: UBS on Amazon: Street’s AWS margin estimates for 2027 are too low Yahoo Finance Australia
trechos: Investing.com -- UBS raised its price target on Amazon to $348 from $318 and reiterated its Buy rating ahead of third-quarter results on Oct.
29, telling investors that Wall Street is underestimating Amazon Web Services margins.

Analyst Stephen Ju said the stock's lack of follow-through after second-quarter results reflects investors pricing in higher 2027 capex of more than $300 billion, which would leave free cash flow at zero or negative.
UBS forecasts a 46% AWS operating margin in 2027, compared with consensus of 38%.
"Our answer is equally as straightforward: they cannot spend the revenue dollars fast enough," he wrote.
UBS stated that AWS is set to add about $80 billion in revenue and $20 billion in depreciation and amortization.
The bank added that to keep margins at the second quarter's roughly 39%, Amazon would need about $29 billion in extra SG&A spending, three times the pace planned for 2026.

"We therefore believe that investors will be forced to raise margin forecasts as Amazon reports each successive quarter, driving what should be higher EPS and FCF forecasts for 2027 and beyond," Ju said.
